extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, hospital finance staff, Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), hospital regulatory/compliance officers, and stakeholders submitting comments on IPPS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and methodological criteria for calculating the uncompensated care Factor 3, trimming potentially aberrant Worksheet S-10 data, interim per-discharge uncompensated care payments, MS-DRG postacute care transfer and special payment inclusion, and the IPPS hospital update for FY 2027. Intended to guide hospitals, MACs, and commenters on data, timing, and thresholds used in payment calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCC trim methodology for potentially aberrant high UCC ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hospital reports an extremely high ratio (greater than 50 percent) of uncompensated care costs to total operating costs in the applicable fiscal year, CMS will determine the ratio of uncompensated care costs to total operating costs from another available cost report and apply that ratio to the total operating expenses for the potentially aberrant fiscal year to determine an adjusted amount of uncompensated care costs for the applicable fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is applied to identify/adjust aberrant uncompensated care (UCC) observations. Audited Worksheet S-10 data are generally exempted (see audited-data exemption). If a hospital would be trimmed under both the UCC trim and the alternative insured-charity trim, the alternative trim is applied in place of the UCC trim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from UCC trim for audited Worksheet S-10 data
rubrics_metrics.description: Worksheet S-10 data that have been audited are not subject to the UCC trim methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because audited Worksheet S-10 data have been subject to audit, CMS has increased confidence in their accuracy and therefore deems it unnecessary to apply the UCC trim methodology for a fiscal year for which a hospital's UCC data have been audited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative trim for potentially aberrant insured patients' charity care costs
rubrics_metrics.description: For hospitals without audited Worksheet S-10 data, if insured patients' charity care costs for a fiscal year are greater than $7 million AND the ratio of the hospital's cost of insured patient charity care (line 23 column 2) to total uncompensated care costs (line 30) is greater than 60 percent, CMS will not calculate a Factor 3 for the hospital at the time of proposed or final rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This trim applies only to hospitals that are not currently projected to be DSH-eligible (thus not part of Factor 3 denominator). If a hospital is trimmed by both this alternative trim and the UCC trim, CMS applies the alternative trim instead. CMS believes the alternative trim better addresses potentially aberrant insured patient charity care because the UCC trim is based solely on the ratio of total UCC to total operating costs and does not consider the level of insured patients' charity care costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and dollar thresholds to identify aberrant insured-patient charity care
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses a threshold of 3 standard deviations from the mean ratio of insured patients' charity care costs to total uncompensated care costs, and a dollar threshold equal to the median total uncompensated care cost reported on the most recent audited cost reports for hospitals projected to be DSH-eligible, to identify potentially aberrant data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS continues to include Worksheet S-10 data from IHS/Tribal hospitals and Puerto Rico hospitals. CMS also applies the same threshold amounts originally calculated for FY 2019 to identify potentially aberrant data for FY 2025 and subsequent fiscal years to facilitate transparency and predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of most recent three years of audited cost reports to calculate Factor 3
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027, Factor 3 is determined using the most recent 3 years of audited cost reports (FYs 2021, 2022, and 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies the same methodology as prior years (e.g., FY 2024) and also applies the scaling factor, new hospital and newly merged hospital policies, CCR trim, UCC trim, and alternative trim policies. The March 2026 HCRIS extract will be used to calculate the final Factor 3 for the FY 2027 final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 step 1: selection of cost reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the hospital's longest cost report for each of the most recent 3 years of audited cost reports. If the hospital has no cost report for a particular year because the prior-year cost report spanned the more recent fiscal year, use the prior-year cost report. If using a previous fiscal year cost report results in a period without a report, use the prior-year report that spans the applicable period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Factor 3 purposes, references to a fiscal year cost report mean the cost report that spans the relevant fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 step 2: annualize uncompensated care costs and use statewide average CCR as needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Annualize the UCC from Worksheet S-10, Part I, Line 30 if a cost report is more than or less than 12 months. If applicable, use the statewide average cost-to-charge ratio (CCR) (urban or rural) to calculate uncompensated care costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures comparability across cost reporting periods of differing lengths and addresses missing or nonrepresentative CCRs by substituting a statewide average CCR where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 step 3: combine UCCs for merged hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine adjusted and/or annualized uncompensated care costs for hospitals that merged using the CMS merger policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merged hospitals' historical UCCs are aggregated per CMS merger policy before inclusion in Factor 3 computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 step 4: calculate Factor 3 for DSH-eligible hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate Factor 3 for all DSH-eligible hospitals using annualized uncompensated care costs (Worksheet S-10, Part I, Line 30) based on cost report data from the most recent 3 years of audited cost reports (from Steps 1–3). Exclude new hospitals and hospitals treated as new for Factor 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New hospitals and those treated as new are excluded from the calculation of Factor 3 when averaging across reporting periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 step 5: averaging and application of scaling factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Average the Factor 3 values from Step 4 (sum the Factor 3 values and divide by the number of cost reporting periods with data) to compute an average Factor 3 for the hospital. Multiply by a scaling factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This produces the hospital's final Factor 3 used to determine uncompensated care payment amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 calculation for hospitals trimmed at rule publication but later DSH-eligible at settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hospital was subject to a trim (UCC or alternative) at rule publication but is ultimately determined to be DSH-eligible at cost report settlement, the MAC will calculate the hospital's Factor 3 only after reviewing the uncompensated care information reported on Worksheet S-10 of the hospital's FY 2027 cost report. The numerator will reflect the uncompensated care costs reported on the hospital's FY 2027 cost report, and the denominator will reflect the sum of the uncompensated care costs reported on Worksheet S-10 of the FY 2023 cost reports of all DSH-eligible hospitals. A scaling factor will be applied to this calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure ensures that hospitals trimmed from the initial publicized calculation but later found eligible are given a Factor 3 calculated from their audited FY 2027 data and the settled denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR trim methodology (use of statewide average CCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the CCR trim methodology, when necessary CMS applies the statewide average CCR to hospital cost reports for purposes of the Factor 3 calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reported counts of hospitals and years where the statewide average CCR was applied (e.g., applied to a number of FY 2021, FY 2022, and FY 2023 reports). The statewide average CCR (urban or rural) is a substitute when a hospital-specific CCR is missing or otherwise not usable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for amended/reopened Worksheet S-10 reports to be included in Factor 3
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Factor 3 calculation for the FY 2027 final rule, any amended reports and/or reopened reports must have completed the amended report and/or reopened report submission processes by the end of March 2026 to be included in the March HCRIS extract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amended/reopened report is not available for the March HCRIS extract, that data will not be part of the FY 2027 Factor 3 calculation. The March HCRIS extract will be available during the comment period so providers can verify inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim per-discharge uncompensated care payment calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim uncompensated care payments are made on a per-discharge basis using a 3-year average of the number of discharges for a hospital to estimate the per-discharge amount. Specifically, the hospital's total uncompensated care payment amount for the fiscal year is divided by the hospital's historical 3-year average of discharges computed using the most recent available data to determine the per-discharge uncompensated care payment for that fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodology has been used since FY 2014 and codified at 42 CFR 412.106(i)(1). Interim payments are reconciled after the fiscal year to ensure final payment consistency with the hospital's prospectively determined uncompensated care payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary MAC request process to reduce per-discharge interim payments
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital may submit a request to its MAC for a lower per-discharge interim uncompensated care payment amount (including reduction to zero) once before the beginning of the fiscal year and/or once during the fiscal year. The hospital must provide supporting documentation demonstrating that there would likely be a significant recoupment at cost report settlement if the per-discharge amount is not lowered (e.g., recoupment of 10 percent or more of the hospital's total uncompensated care payment, or at least $100,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable documentation: projected large increase in discharges, or interim payments already surpassing total uncompensated care payment. The MAC will evaluate requests and supporting documentation and, if it agrees significant recoupment is likely, will lower the per-discharge amount to the amount requested or another amount the MAC deems appropriate. Any updated per-discharge amount will be used for outlier payment calculations for the remainder of the fiscal year. Lowering the per-discharge amount does not change the total uncompensated care payment amount determined by Factor 3 (reconciliation occurs at cost report settlement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and review process for Factor 3 tables and supplemental data
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will publish on its website a table listing Factor 3 for hospitals estimated to receive empirically justified Medicare DSH payments in FY 2027 and a supplemental data file containing a list of known mergers and computed uncompensated care payments for merged hospitals. New hospitals and hospitals subject to the alternative trim and not projected to be DSH-eligible will have N/A in the Factor 3 column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals have 60 days from public display of the proposed rule in the Federal Register to review these files and notify CMS in writing of issues related to mergers or potential upload discrepancies due to MAC mishandling of Worksheet S-10 data during report submission. Comments about mergers/upload discrepancies should be emailed to Section3133DSH@cms.hhs.gov. The CMS DSH inbox is not intended for Worksheet S-10 audit process emails (those should go to MACs). All other comments must follow submission methods in the ADDRESSES section to be assured consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and per-diem calculation for transfers under §412.4(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discharges under IPPS include cases where a patient is formally released or dies. When a patient is transferred and length of stay is less than the geometric mean length of stay for the MS-DRG, the transferring hospital is generally paid based on a graduated per diem rate for each day of stay, not to exceed the full MS-DRG payment. The per diem rate is calculated by dividing the full MS-DRG payment by the geometric mean length of stay for the MS-DRG. CMS generally provides payment that is twice the per diem amount for the first day, with each subsequent day paid at the per diem amount up to the full MS-DRG payment (§412.4(f)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer cases are also eligible for outlier payments. This per-diem structure reflects evidence that the first day of hospitalization is the most expensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlier threshold formula for transfer cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The outlier threshold for transfer cases is equal to (Fixed-Loss Outlier threshold for Nontransfer Cases adjusted for geographic variations in costs / Geometric Mean Length of Stay for the MS-DRG) * (Length of Stay for the Case plus 1 day) (§412.80(b) referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formula adjusts the outlier threshold to account for transfer case length of stay and geographic cost differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for including an MS-DRG on the postacute care transfer policy list (§412.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS applies the postacute care transfer policy to an MS-DRG (and any other MS-DRG that shares the same base MS-DRG) if (1) the MS-DRG's total number of discharges to postacute care equals or exceeds the 55th percentile for all MS-DRGs, and (2) the proportion of short-stay discharges to postacute care to total discharges in the MS-DRG exceeds the 55th percentile for all MS-DRGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considers the statute's direction to identify MS-DRGs based on a high volume of discharges to postacute care and disproportionate use of postacute care services. CMS concluded the 55th percentile is an appropriate threshold. CMS will not revise the list annually unless making a change to a specific MS-DRG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special payment methodology criteria for MS-DRGs (§412.4(f)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: An MS-DRG qualifies for the special payment methodology (to address exceptionally higher shares of costs early in the stay) if the geometric mean length of stay is greater than 4 days AND the average charges of 1-day discharge cases in the MS-DRG are at least 50 percent of the average charges for all cases within the MS-DRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For qualifying MS-DRGs, hospitals receive 50 percent of the full MS-DRG payment plus the single per diem payment for the first day, as well as a per diem payment for subsequent days (up to the full MS-DRG payment). MS-DRGs that share the same base MS-DRG will all qualify if any one of them qualifies (applies to severity level groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of current Medicare GROUPER and most recent complete MedPAR data for DRG determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a DRG did not exist in Medicare Version 23.0 or a DRG in Version 23.0 is revised, CMS uses the current version of the Medicare GROUPER and the most recent complete year of MedPAR data to determine if the DRG is subject to the postacute care transfer policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures DRG inclusion/exclusion assessments reflect current coding and utilization patterns when DRG definitions change.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5 percent case-shift threshold to trigger reassessment of affected MS-DRGs
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS evaluates any current MS-DRG if it estimates that more than 5 percent of the current cases would shift from the current assigned MS-DRGs to proposed new MS-DRGs, or to a current MS-DRG from a proposed revised or deleted MS-DRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the >5% threshold is met, CMS reassesses the MS-DRG to determine whether it should be subject to the postacute care transfer policy (and evaluates special payment methodology criteria where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when an MS-DRG qualifies for postacute care transfer policy or special payment method
rubrics_metrics.description: If an MS-DRG qualifies for the postacute care transfer policy or the special payment methodology, CMS proposes adding that MS-DRG (and related MS-DRGs that share the same base MS-DRG) to the respective lists effective for the fiscal year (e.g., proposed additions for FY 2027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS evaluates proposed new and revised MS-DRGs using the most recent MedPAR data available at proposal and will update analysis for the final rule using the most recent data at that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable percentage increase to IPPS standardized amount and statutory reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable percentage increase for the IPPS standardized amount equals the rate-of-increase in the hospital market basket, subject to the following reductions applied in sequence: (A) reduction of one-quarter of the applicable percentage increase for hospitals failing to submit quality information; (B) reduction of three-quarters of the applicable percentage increase for hospitals not considered meaningful EHR users; and (C) an adjustment based on changes in economy-wide multifactor productivity (the productivity adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The productivity adjustment is defined as the 10-year moving average of changes in annual economy-wide private nonfarm business multifactor productivity as projected by the Secretary; application may result in the applicable percentage increase being less than zero. CMS proposes to base the FY 2027 market basket update on IGI's Q4 2025 forecast (estimated 3.2%) and to propose a productivity adjustment of 0.8% (IGI forecast). If more recent data become available, CMS may use them for the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market basket rebasing frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS rebases the hospital market basket every 4 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS replaced the 2018-based market baskets with rebased and revised 2023-based operating and capital market baskets beginning in FY 2026. Consistent with the 4-year frequency, CMS plans to propose rebasing and revision in the FY 2030 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updates to hospital-specific rates for SCHs and MDHs based on quality submission and EHR meaningful-use status
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027 CMS proposes specific updates to SCH/MDH hospital-specific rates depending on whether the hospital submits quality data and whether it is a meaningful EHR user: 2.4 percent for a hospital that submits quality data and is a meaningful EHR user; 0.0 percent for a hospital that submits quality data and is not a meaningful EHR user; 1.6 percent for a hospital that fails to submit quality data and is a meaningful EHR user; and −0.8 percent for a hospital that fails to submit quality data and is not a meaningful EHR user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These proposed percentages reflect applying the market basket rate-of-increase and the statutory reductions (including the productivity adjustment) to produce the applicable percentage increases for different hospital categories.
